  "required_fixes": [
    "[P1] RF01 — Do not present content-level scan failures as Allow. crates/desktop-core/src/scanning.rs:233 considers only timeout and the global error flag when determining incompleteness. A schema-valid reply with action=allow, category=benign, timeout=false, error=false and errors=[{content_type:prompt,feature:dlp,status:error}] consequently becomes Verdict::Allow. The pinned SDK schema does not require the global flag to agree with errors. apps/desktop/src/features/runtime/runtime-view.tsx:278 also hides those content errors unless serviceError is true, producing a green Allowed result without the failure details. Classify content-level errors or contradictory completion indicators conservatively and display the relevant partial/error information independently of that global flag. Acceptance: add a literal endpoint response with this combination through production authority/SDK tests and the production React result view; it must never appear Allowed, and the failed content/detector must be visible.",
    "[P2] RF02 — Preserve uncertainty about transmission in operator text. apps/desktop/src/features/runtime/scan-text.ts:108–111 says 'The request was sent' and 'Cancelled after it was sent' for every Unknown outcome. The implementation correctly maps connect failures to Unknown, and DispatchClaimed/cancellation does not prove bytes reached the service. The text therefore asserts evidence the native outcome does not establish. Use wording that permits both sent and not-sent possibilities unless separate positive transmission evidence is available. Acceptance: cover a connection failure before transmission and cancellation after claiming but before transport send; both retain Unknown where appropriate, disclose possible remote execution, avoid asserting successful transmission and never replay automatically."
  ],
  "blockers": [],
  "evidence_gaps": [
    "The submitted C03 runs do not include current-source regressions for C02's context_credentials or the applicable desktop-host ipc_admission suite. C03 changes shared authority/context retirement, session ownership, cancellation publication and the Receipt/ShellSnapshot wire shape; common checks compile targets but run only core library and frontend tests. The C02 receipt binds the earlier tree. Rerun and retain the affected authority/IPC regressions against the repaired C03 fingerprints, as required by chunks/C03.md's earlier-chunk regression instruction."
  ],
  "optional_suggestions": [],
  "limitations": [
    "Independently recomputed all four fingerprints and verified source inventory, packet references, tool executable hashes, run-log hashes, fixture executable/bundle hashes, production app tree and DMG hashes. All matched. Verified the passing C02 receipt/verdict/raw-output hashes, completion record and base-commit ancestry.",
    "Retained results report 71 frontend, 26 core and 13 sync-scan tests passing; the 14 targeted scan-submit frontend cases overlap the 71. Independently reran the existing 13-test sync_scan executable against its own synthetic loopback TLS servers; all passed. An in-memory execution of the production scan-text module confirmed RF02's current wording. RF01 follows from production mapping/UI code and the pinned SDK response schema; its counterexample is absent from the supplied tests.",
    "Acknowledgement: budgets.json versions 2 and 3 may use the recorded revised input methods for the narrowly defined scan-memory workload. Numeric limits remain unchanged, failed version-2 evidence is retained, and version 3 was registered before its acceptance run. This acknowledgement does not close or waive the long typed-input/assistive-client memory problem assigned to C24.",
    "Recomputed current budget statistics: cold p95 572.172 ms, warm p95 322.545 ms, input proxy p95 21.206 ms, idle max 206.516 MiB, scan max 315.906 MiB, unsigned app 15.992 MiB and DMG 5.973 MiB; all meet the registered limits and sample counts. Input-to-paint is an accessibility-value timing proxy plus an assumed frame, not captured compositor timing; cold runs do not purge OS file caches.",
    "Native acceptance is implementer-recorded fixture evidence with 12 passing checks. No native UI or performance run was repeated by the reviewer. No application source was changed, real credentials accessed or product endpoints called; only designated review artifacts were written. Fixture trust roots are compile-gated; live service qualification and signed installed-package validation remain C25/C26, and P01 still requires its cumulative review."
  ],
